McLaren: McLaren has fitted a circuit‑specific, high‑flow front brake duct to boost cooling on the front brakes. This means the brakes stay at optimal temperatures longer, letting the drivers brake later and harder into the corners without losing grip. The extra cooling could be the edge that keeps them competitive on a track where brake temperature is a big factor this weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes have reshaped the front wing, moving to a slimmer, two‑piece layout and re‑balancing the wing’s surface area. They also tweaked the endplates, footplate and dive‑plane angles to keep the airflow smoother around the front tires. The result should be a stickier front end, giving the car better turn‑in and stability on the upcoming circuit.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has tweaked the front wing, reshaping the outer pieces and flaps to give the car a steadier bite on the corner‑entry aerodynamics, which should translate into more consistent grip as the track heats up. They’ve also widened the exit duct on the rear‑wheel bodywork to keep the rear more reliable under high loads, helping the power unit stay cool and avoid overheating. Together, these changes aim to boost stability and keep the car running flat‑out through the whole weekend.
